newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Short term optimism keeps Singapore shares firm.
newsitem.headline: Short term optimism keeps Singapore shares firm.

text.p: Buying into laggard blue chip stocks and short term optimism fuelled by good performances on foreign stock markets held Singapore share prices firm on Monday, dealers said.
"We're seeing short term optimism based on the strength of overseas markets," one local dealer said.
"The markets around the world are positive so there's no reason why we shouldn't adopt this view too," said another.
At 0228 GMT, Singapore's benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was up 8.88 points at 2,203.63. Overall, 178 gainers beat 40 losers on market volume of 67.78 million units.

The bulk of the turnover was from the debut of interior design and furniture firm, Nobel Design, which saw 24.98 million shares change hands by 0228 GMT. They hit a high of Singapore $0.55 and stood at S$047.5, 44 percent above its offer price of S$0.33.

Besides Nobel's debut, dealers said laggard blue chips would be the main attraction for buyers on Monday. Mid to low capitalised stocks, such as hotel groups, were likely to be targets, said a dealer.
Malaysian over the counter stocks were firmer with the UOB OTC index up 7.67 points at 1,228.70.
